title: Protocol to Analyze Transmigration of Human Cytotoxic T Cells Under Physiological Flow Conditions In Vitro
author: Schoppmeyer, van Buul
materials: Timing: 1 h before start of the experiment

steps.title: Prepare cold buffers and dilute blood
steps.instruction: Keep all buffers on ice. Prepare PBMC buffer (PBS + 2 mM EDTA, cold) and CTL isolation buffer (PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5 % FCS, cold). Dilute fresh heparinised blood 1:1 with the cold PBMC buffer.

steps.title: Layer blood over Ficoll and centrifuge
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL conical bottom tube add 15 mL Ficoll Paque PLUS, then carefully layer 35 mL of the diluted blood on top without mixing. Centrifuge at 400 g for 40 min at room temperature (RT) with no brake (acceleration can stay on high).

steps.title: Harvest PBMC layer and wash cells
steps.instruction: Remove the upper plasma layer until 5–10 mL of plasma remain above the white PBMC ring. Aspirate the PBMC ring into a fresh tube and bring the volume to 50 mL with cold PBMC buffer. Centrifuge at 350 g for 10 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 50 mL PBMC buffer and centrifuge again at 200 g for 10 min. Take an aliquot to count cells, then repeat the 200 g wash once more. After the final spin discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in the CTL isolation buffer supplied with the Miltenyi CD8⁺ isolation kit.

steps.title: Isolate CD8⁺ T cells with Miltenyi kit
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the Miltenyi CD8⁺ isolation kit using LS columns and the prepared CTL isolation buffer (PBS + 2 mM EDTA + 0.5 % FCS, cold).

steps.title: Recover CTL in culture overnight
steps.instruction: Resuspend isolated CD8⁺ T cells in recovery medium (RPMI‑1640 + 10 % FCS + 1 % Pen/Strep + 10 mM HEPES). Adjust cell density to 2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Note: Do not start with fewer than 10 × 10⁶ PBMC; assume a 5 % yield to guarantee ≥1 × 10⁶ CTL per flow channel.

steps.title: Place flow chamber on microscope
steps.instruction: Mount the μ‑channel slide containing the inflamed endothelial monolayer on a phase‑contrast microscope. Fix the slide, remove the lid and shift the lid aside to cover only the channel that will be imaged, protecting the other channels from evaporation and contamination.

steps.title: Connect tubing and clamps
steps.instruction: Attach flow tubing (pump → channel → liquid container) using the clamps shown in Figure 2A. Unlock clamps, connect the pump to one side and the HEPES⁺ buffer reservoir to the opposite side. Flush the tubing (previously stored in 70 % ethanol) sequentially with 50 mL sterile water, 50 mL PBS, and 50 mL HEPES⁺ buffer, using a high flow rate of 10 mL min⁻¹ (no cells present). Clamp the tubing on both sides, then apply excess buffer volume to the inlet chambers of the selected channel.

steps.title: Attach Luer connectors and remove air
steps.instruction: Remove the short connector piece (green #). Connect the Luer connectors from the pump side and the buffer‑container side directly to the channel. Flush each Luer connector of trapped air by inserting a 200 µL pipette tip, filling it with HEPES⁺ buffer, and holding the opening upward before tightening the connection. Ensure no air bubbles are introduced; any bubble at the pump side will be flushed away, but bubbles at the channel inlet can damage the monolayer.

steps.title: Prime endothelial monolayer with flow
steps.instruction: Run HEPES⁺ buffer through the channel at an estimated shear stress of ~0.7 dyne cm⁻² for at least 10 min. Avoid any air inclusion during this step; if bubbles appear, stop flow, disconnect the Luer connector, and re‑flush with buffer before reconnecting.

steps.title: Prepare CTL suspension for injection
steps.instruction: Tap air out of the syringe containing the CTL suspension, then load the syringe into the pump line, taking care not to introduce bubbles that could reach the monolayer.

steps.title: Open image series in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Launch ImageJ (or Fiji) and open the saved time‑lapse image series of the flow channel.

steps.title: Set up counting tool and Excel file
steps.instruction: Open the ImageJ counting tool and create a new Excel spreadsheet to record all counts and calculations.

steps.title: Count adherent cells at series end
steps.instruction: Move the time slider to the final frame, use the counting tool to mark and count all adherent CTL (group 1). Save the total adherent count in the Excel file.

steps.title: Identify and count transmigrated cells
steps.instruction: Play the time‑lapse from start to finish, following each adherent cell. When a cell shows a phase‑contrast change from bright to dark and remains dark (indicating it is underneath the endothelium), mark its transmigration spot with the counting tool (group 2). Record the number of transmigration events (both local and distant) in Excel.

steps.title: Determine junctions crossed per cell
steps.instruction: For each transmigrated cell, count how many EC‑EC junctions it crossed from its initial adhesion point. Cells crossing more than one junction are classified as distant diapedesis events. Compute: # distant = count of cells crossing > 1 junction; # local = # total − # distant. Calculate frequency of distant diapedesis = (# distant / # total) × 100 %.

steps.title: Classify local migration routes
steps.instruction: For each locally transmigrated cell, decide whether the route is transcellular (rounded phenotype, no apical migration) or paracellular (occurs at EC‑EC junctions, preceded by a polarized phenotype). Record numbers of transcellular and paracellular events and calculate: % transcellular = (# transcellular / # local) × 100 %; % paracellular = 100 % − % transcellular.

steps.title: Count unpolarized adherent cells
steps.instruction: Identify adherent CTL that are rounded but neither transmigrated nor apically migrating. Record this number (group 3). Compute unpolarized fraction = (# unpolarized / # adherent) × 100 %. Compute polarized‑but‑not‑transmigrated fraction = (# adherent − # transmigrated − # unpolarized) / # adherent × 100 %.

steps.title: Calculate overall transmigration metrics
steps.instruction:
Using the counts recorded, calculate: Transmigration efficiency = (# transmigrated / # adherent) × 100 %; Frequency of distant diapedesis = (# distant / # transmigrated) × 100 %; Transcellular route frequency = (# transcellular / # local) × 100 %; Paracellular route frequency = 100 % − Transcellular %.
Save all results in the Excel file.
